literal: My lord before do not stand, O enemies! Many, my lord before having stood, stone stood.
translation: O enemies, do not stand before my lord! Many who stood before him now stand only as hero-stones.
modern: பகைவர்களே! என் தலைவனுக்கு முன்னால் வந்து நிற்காதீர்கள். என் தலைவனுக்கு முன்னால் வந்து எதிர்த்து நின்ற பலர், இன்று நடுகல்லாகத்தான் நிற்கிறார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet expresses the fierce pride of a warrior boasting about his leader's might. He warns the enemies not to stand in battle against his lord ('என்னை'). The word 'ஐ' here means leader or lord. He reminds them that many brave men who previously dared to stand against his lord were slain and now exist only as 'hero-stones' (நடுகல்) erected in their memory. The play on the word 'stand' (நின்று, நின்றவர்) contrasts standing in battle with standing eternally as a stone monument.
